title: One Law, Two Exact Nulls: what coherence measures, and what it cannot certify
description:
A synthesis of two independently-run hardware programmes. It contains no new measurements. Its contribution is the identification that its two companion programmes measured the same function, and the demonstration that their two internal nulls, taken together, settle what that function certifies.

One law. cos(theta/2) is the overlap between two qubit states separated by Bloch angle theta. Both programmes measure coherence surviving as a product of those overlaps, one factor per party that has acquired distinguishing information. twisted-spin-ptm measures it against COUPLING ANGLE (T_xx = cos(chi_t/2)^(N-2), the exponent counting N-2 bulk spins); relational-time-ibm-quantum measures the same overlap against TIME (rho_C = cos((t-t')pi/d)) and against environment coupling (cos(mu/2)^p). The identification is exact, not analogical: adjacent clock records at d=8 overlap at 0.923880, and cos(pi/4 / 2) = 0.923880. Entanglement decay and temporal distinguishability are the same bookkeeping read in different variables.

Two exact nulls. Each programme has a structural zero that was predicted from theory, pre-registered, and confirmed on hardware -- the internal controls that validated each apparatus. At chi_t = pi the OAT boundary observable reads exactly 0.000000 on a state that is I/4 with concurrence 0, SEPARABLE. At d = 2 the relational-time witness reads exactly 0.000000 on a Bell pair carrying 1.0000 ebits, MAXIMALLY ENTANGLED. The same observable reads exactly zero at both extremes of the entanglement spectrum. This is a measurement of entanglement-blindness, not an argument for it, and neither repository can demonstrate it alone.

The convergent resolution. Both programmes hit the same wall from opposite directions and neither anticipated the other's version: entanglement is not identifiable from PTM anisotropy alone, resolved by V_Q over Haar-random settings; and no single local product-basis distribution certifies clock-system entanglement, resolved by a multi-setting fidelity witness after two adversarial states beat the single-setting ones. Certification of quantum structure requires agreement across incompatible measurements.

Applied bounds. The line began with two engineering questions about moving information off a spacecraft, and both now have derived negative answers: Holevo and superdense coding bound the payload so compression must be earned classically before encoding, and relativistic time dilation trades local throughput for Earth-frame storage rather than accelerating computation, at gamma-1 ~ 1e-10 in practice.

Claim boundary: no new measurements; nothing about quantum electrodynamics (no gauge field, photon or vacuum appears in either programme); nothing about whether time in nature is emergent. Both states are prepared by externally timed gates and both clock/system splits are imposed rather than derived. Not peer-reviewed.
notes: Synthesis of two companion programmes; contains no new measurements.
